hci_h4.direction: Indicates the flow of a Host Controller Interface (HCI) packet, specifying if it's being sent from the host to the controller or received from the controller by the host.
hci_h4.type: Specifies the packet type for HCI communication over a UART H4 interface, such as Command, ACL Data, SCO Data, or Event.
h4bcm.type: Defines the category of proprietary Broadcom diagnostic information being transmitted over the H4 transport layer.
h4bcm.clock: Represents the native clock value of the master Bluetooth device, used for synchronization and debugging purposes in Broadcom diagnostic logs.
h4bcm.maclow: Contains the Lower Address Part (LAP) of the Bluetooth device's MAC address within a Broadcom diagnostic message.
h4bcm.pldhdr: Indicates the header for the payload section of a Broadcom-specific diagnostic packet.
h4bcm.aclhdr: Represents the standard Asynchronous Connection-Less (ACL) data header encapsulated within a Broadcom diagnostic message.
h4bcm.llid: The Logical Link ID field identifies whether the packet fragment is the start of a new L2CAP message or a continuation of a current one.
h4bcm.llid_acl: The Logical Link ID specifically for an ACL packet, indicating if it's the start or continuation of an L2CAP message.
h4bcm.flow_acl: A flag within an ACL packet's header indicating the flow control state, such as go (flow is on) or stop (flow is off).
h4bcm.rfu_acl: Reserved for Future Use; a field in the ACL header that is not currently defined and should be ignored.
h4bcm.flow: A flag that indicates the flow control status for the data payload, signaling whether the device is permitted to send more data.
h4bcm.length: Specifies the total length of the payload data that follows the header.
h4bcm.length_acl: Specifies the length of the payload data within an ACL packet.
h4bcm.payload: The actual data content being transmitted in the packet.
h4bcm.acl_fragment: The data payload portion of a fragmented ACL packet.
h4bcm.logging: Contains logging data from the Link Manager (LM) for both BR/EDR and Low Energy (LE) operations.
h4bcm.stats.null_rcvd: A counter for the total number of NULL-type packets that have been successfully received.
h4bcm.stats.poll_rcvd: A counter for the total number of POLL-type packets that have been successfully received.
h4bcm.stats.dm1_rcvd: A counter for the number of received Data Medium Rate (DM1) packets, which provide error correction.
h4bcm.stats.dh1_rcvd: A counter for the number of received Data High Rate (DH1) packets, which do not have error correction but offer higher data rates.
h4bcm.stats.dv_rcvd: A counter for the received Data-Voice (DV) packets, which contain both data and synchronous voice data.
h4bcm.stats.aux1_rcvd: A counter for the total number of AUX1-type packets that have been successfully received.
h4bcm.stats.dm3_rcvd: A counter for the number of received 3-slot Data Medium Rate (DM3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dh3_rcvd: A counter for the number of received 3-slot Data High Rate (DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dm5_rcvd: A counter for the number of received 5-slot Data Medium Rate (DM5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dh5_rcvd: A counter for the number of received 5-slot Data High Rate (DH5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.null_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted NULL-type packets.
h4bcm.stats.poll_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted POLL-type packets.
h4bcm.stats.dm1_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted Data Medium Rate (DM1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dh1_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted Data High Rate (DH1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dv_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted Data-Voice (DV) packets.
h4bcm.stats.aux1_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted AUX1-type packets.
h4bcm.stats.dm3_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted 3-slot Data Medium Rate (DM3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dh3_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted 3-slot Data High Rate (DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dm5_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted 5-slot Data Medium Rate (DM5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.dh5_tx: A counter for the total number of transmitted 5-slot Data High Rate (DH5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.acl_rx: A cumulative count of the total number of ACL data bytes received by the device.
h4bcm.stats.acl_tx: A cumulative count of the total number of ACL data bytes transmitted by the device.
h4bcm.stats.hec_err: Counts the number of packets received with a Header Error Check (HEC) failure, indicating corruption in the packet header.
h4bcm.stats.crc_err: Counts the number of packets received with a Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) failure, indicating corruption in the packet payload.
h4bcm.stats.seqn_rep: A counter for how many times a packet with a duplicate sequence number was received, indicating a retransmission.
h4bcm.stats.soft_rst: A counter for the number of times a soft reset has occurred on the Bluetooth controller.
h4bcm.stats.test_tx: A counter for the number of packets transmitted while the device is in a specific test mode.
h4bcm.stats.test_rx: A counter for the number of packets received while the device is in a specific test mode.
h4bcm.stats.test_err: A counter for packet errors that occurred while the device was operating in test mode.
h4bcm.stats.2dh1_rcvd: A counter for received 1-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh1_rcvd: A counter for received 1-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.2dh3_rcvd: A counter for received 3-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh3_rcvd: A counter for received 3-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.2dh5_rcvd: A counter for received 5-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh5_rcvd: A counter for received 5-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.2dh1_tx: A counter for transmitted 1-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh1_tx: A counter for transmitted 1-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH1) packets.
h4bcm.stats.2dh3_tx: A counter for transmitted 3-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh3_tx: A counter for transmitted 3-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH3) packets.
h4bcm.stats.2dh5_tx: A counter for transmitted 5-slot, 2-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (2-DH5) packets.
h4bcm.stats.3dh5_tx: A counter for transmitted 5-slot, 3-Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (3-DH5) packets.
h4bcm.le.address: The 48-bit device address of the remote Bluetooth Low Energy device in the connection.
h4bcm.le.handle: The connection handle, a unique identifier for a specific connection with a Bluetooth LE device.
h4bcm.le.opcode: The operation code that specifies the command or event being sent in a Broadcom-specific LE packet.
h4bcm.le.opcodeext: A Broadcom-specific operation code that extends the standard set of LE opcodes for proprietary features.
h4bcm.le.versnr: The version number of the Broadcom LE feature or protocol being used.
h4bcm.le.subversnr: The subversion number, providing more granular version information for a Broadcom LE feature.
h4bcm.le.compid: The company identifier, which for these packets identifies Broadcom.
btbbd: Encapsulates a raw Bluetooth baseband packet, representing the physical layer of communication.
btbbd.meta: Contains supplementary information about the baseband packet, such as signal strength (RSSI), channel, and timing.
btbbd.clk: The value of the native clock (CLKN) when the packet was captured, used for timing analysis.
btbbd.ch: The specific frequency channel (from 0 to 78) on which the baseband packet was transmitted or received.
btbbd.ptt: The Packet Type Table, which determines the types of packets (e.g., DM1, DH3) that can be used on the logical link.
btbbd.role: Indicates the device's role in the piconet at the time of transmission, either Master or Slave.
btbbd.txenc: A flag indicating whether the transmitted baseband packet is encrypted.
btbbd.rxenc: A flag indicating whether the received baseband packet is encrypted.
btbbd.iseir: A flag indicating if this packet is part of an Extended Inquiry Response (EIR), providing more data during device discovery.
btbbd.pkthdr: The header of the baseband packet, containing fields like LT_ADDR, packet type, and flow control bits.
btbbd.lt_addr: The Logical Transport Address, a 3-bit address assigned to an active device within a piconet.
btbbd.type: Identifies the type of the baseband packet (e.g., ID, NULL, POLL, FHS, DM1).
btbbd.type_br: Specifies the packet type for Basic Rate (BR) communications.
btbbd.type_edr: Specifies the packet type for Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) communications.
btbbd.flow: A 1-bit flow control flag used to stop and start the flow of ACL data packets from the other device.
btbbd.arqn: The Automatic Retransmission Request Number, a 1-bit acknowledgement field to indicate if the last packet was received successfully.
btbbd.seqn: The Sequence Number, a 1-bit field that toggles for each new data packet to detect retransmissions.
btbbd.hec: The Header Error Check field, an 8-bit value used to detect errors in the packet's access code and header.
fhs: A Frequency Hopping Selection packet, which is used to synchronize a new device to the master's timing and frequency hopping pattern.
fhs.parity: Contains the parity bits calculated from various fields within the FHS packet for error checking.
fhs.lap: The Lower Address Part of the master device's Bluetooth Address (BD_ADDR).
fhs.eir: A flag that indicates whether an Extended Inquiry Response (EIR) packet will follow the FHS packet.
fhs.sr: The Scan Repetition mode used by the master during the page scan procedure (e.g., R1, R2).
fhs.uap: The Upper Address Part of the master device's Bluetooth Address (BD_ADDR).
fhs.nap: The Non-significant Address Part of the master device's Bluetooth Address (BD_ADDR).
fhs.class: The Class of Device (CoD), which describes the type and capabilities of the master device (e.g., computer, phone, audio device).
fhs.lt_addr: The Logical Transport Address that will be assigned to the slave device once it joins the piconet.
fhs.clk: Contains bits 27 down to 2 of the master's native clock, used to synchronize the slave device.
btbrlmp.accscheme: Indicates the paging scheme supported by the device, such as interlaced or standard page scans.
btbrlmp.afhchmap: The channel map used for Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH), indicating which channels are in use or blocked.
btbrlmp.afhclass: A report from one device to another classifying channels as 'good' or 'bad' for use with AFH.
btbrlmp.afhinst: The specific clock tick (instant) at which the new Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH) pattern will be applied.
btbrlmp.maxintvl: The maximum interval, in time slots, for an AFH channel map update.
btbrlmp.minintvl: The minimum interval, in time slots, for an AFH channel map update.
btbrlmp.afhmode: A control field to enable or disable the use of Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH).
btbrlmp.afhrptmode: A field to enable or disable the AFH channel classification reporting mode.
btbrlmp.airmode: Specifies the audio coding format used on a SCO/eSCO link, such as μ-Law, A-Law, or CVSD.
btbrlmp.araddr: The anony-mode address (AR_ADDR) is a temporary address assigned to a slave during connectionless slave broadcast.
btbrlmp.authreqs: Specifies the authentication requirements for the connection, such as MITM protection.
btbrlmp.authres: The response sent during an authentication procedure.
btbrlmp.bdaddr: The Bluetooth Device Address of the remote device involved in the LMP transaction.
btbrlmp.bsw: The time duration, in slots, for the broadcast scan window in a connectionless slave broadcast.
btbrlmp.clkoffset: The measured difference between the master's and slave's clocks, used for synchronization.
btbrlmp.commit: A cryptographic commitment value used during Secure Simple Pairing (SSP) to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.
btbrlmp.confirm: A confirmation value exchanged during pairing to verify that both devices have the same key.
btbrlmp.compid: The company identifier assigned by the Bluetooth SIG, indicating the manufacturer of the device's controller.
btbrlmp.cryptmode: The encryption mode for the link, specifying whether encryption is off, for point-to-point traffic only, or for broadcast traffic as well.
btbrlmp.daccess: The time interval, in slots, between the start of two consecutive access windows in sniff mode.
btbrlmp.db: Parameter used in sniff mode calculations.
btbrlmp.dbsleep: The sleep duration parameter used in sniff mode.
btbrlmp.deltab: A parameter, measured in slots, used for sniff mode timing.
btbrlmp.desco: The offset to the start of the eSCO link's reserved slave transmission slot.
btbrlmp.drift: The measured clock drift of the slave device's clock compared to the master's, measured in parts per million (ppm).
btbrlmp.dsco: The interval, in slots, between two consecutive SCO or eSCO connection events.
btbrlmp.dsniff: The interval, in slots, between the start of two consecutive sniff mode listening attempts.
btbrlmp.encdata: The actual data payload that is encapsulated within an LMP message, used for tunneling other protocols.
btbrlmp.enclen: The length of the data that is encapsulated within an LMP message.
btbrlmp.encmaj: The major type identifier for the protocol whose data is encapsulated in the LMP message.
btbrlmp.encmin: The minor type identifier for the protocol whose data is encapsulated in the LMP message.
btbrlmp.eop: The Extended Opcode, which allows for more LMP commands than the standard opcode field permits.
btbrlmp.eopinre: The Extended Opcode of the original request that this LMP message is a response to.
btbrlmp.escolenms: The maximum allowed length, in bytes, of an eSCO packet sent from the Master to the Slave.
btbrlmp.escolensm: The maximum allowed length, in bytes, of an eSCO packet sent from the Slave to the Master.
btbrlmp.escotypems: Defines the eSCO packet types (e.g., EV3, EV4, 2-EV5) that can be used from the Master to the Slave.
btbrlmp.escotypesm: Defines the eSCO packet types that can be used from the Slave to the Master.
btbrlmp.err: The error code indicating the reason for an LMP request failure or rejection.
btbrlmp.escohdl: The handle or identifier for a specific Extended SCO (eSCO) link.
btbrlmp.escoltaddr: The Logical Transport Address assigned specifically to an eSCO link.
btbrlmp.features: A bitmask representing the set of Bluetooth features supported by the local or remote device.
btbrlmp.feat.3slot: A feature bit indicating that the device supports 3-slot baseband packets.
btbrlmp.feat.5slot: A feature bit indicating that the device supports 5-slot baseband packets.
btbrlmp.feat.enc: A feature bit indicating that the device supports link-level encryption.
btbrlmp.feat.slotoff: A feature bit indicating that the device supports the slot offset procedure for timing adjustments.
btbrlmp.feat.timacc: A feature bit that indicates the device can provide timing accuracy information.
btbrlmp.feat.rolesw: A feature bit indicating the device supports switching its role from master to slave (or vice-versa).
btbrlmp.feat.holdmo: A feature bit indicating the device supports Hold mode, a power-saving feature.
btbrlmp.feat.sniffmo: A feature bit indicating the device supports Sniff mode, a power-saving feature.
btbrlmp.feat.res0: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.pwrctlreq: A feature bit indicating the device can request power control adjustments from the other device.
btbrlmp.feat.cqddr: A bit indicating support for Channel Quality Driven Data Rate, where packet types are chosen based on link quality.
btbrlmp.feat.sco: A feature bit indicating the device supports creating Synchronous Connection-Oriented (SCO) links, used for voice.
btbrlmp.feat.hv2: A feature bit indicating support for HV2 (High Quality Voice 2) SCO packets.
btbrlmp.feat.hv3: A feature bit indicating support for HV3 (High Quality Voice 3) SCO packets.
btbrlmp.feat.mulaw: Indicates the device's codec supports μ-law log format for synchronous data.
btbrlmp.feat.alaw: Indicates the device's codec supports A-law log format for synchronous data.
btbrlmp.feat.cvsd: Indicates the device's codec supports CVSD (Continuously Variable Slope Delta) format for synchronous data.
btbrlmp.feat.pagneg: Indicates the device supports negotiating paging scan parameters to optimize connections.
btbrlmp.feat.pwrctl: A feature bit indicating the device supports link-level power control.
btbrlmp.feat.transsync: Indicates the device supports transparently relaying a synchronous data stream.
btbrlmp.feat.flowctl1: The least significant bit of the flow control lag feature.
btbrlmp.feat.flowctl2: The middle bit of the flow control lag feature.
btbrlmp.feat.flowctl3: The most significant bit of the flow control lag feature.
btbrlmp.feat.bcenc: A feature bit indicating the device supports encryption for broadcast packets.
btbrlmp.feat.res1: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.acl2: Indicates the device supports 2 Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) for ACL links.
btbrlmp.feat.acl3: Indicates the device supports 3 Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) for ACL links.
btbrlmp.feat.eninq: A feature bit indicating support for the enhanced inquiry scan procedure.
btbrlmp.feat.intinq: A feature bit indicating support for the interlaced inquiry scan procedure.
btbrlmp.feat.intpag: A feature bit indicating support for the interlaced page scan procedure.
btbrlmp.feat.rssiinq: Indicates the device can provide RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indication) values with its inquiry results.
btbrlmp.feat.ev3: A feature bit indicating support for EV3 Extended SCO (eSCO) packets.
btbrlmp.feat.ev4: A feature bit indicating support for EV4 eSCO packets.
btbrlmp.feat.ev5: A feature bit indicating support for EV5 eSCO packets.
btbrlmp.feat.res2: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.afhcapsl: Indicates a slave device is capable of performing Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH).
btbrlmp.feat.afhclasl: Indicates a slave device is capable of classifying channels for AFH.
btbrlmp.feat.bredrnotsup: Indicates the controller does not support BR/EDR and only supports Low Energy.
btbrlmp.feat.lesup: A feature bit indicating the Bluetooth controller supports Bluetooth Low Energy (LE).
btbrlmp.feat.3slotenh: Indicates the device supports 3-slot ACL packets for Enhanced Data Rate (EDR).
btbrlmp.feat.5slotenh: Indicates the device supports 5-slot ACL packets for Enhanced Data Rate (EDR).
btbrlmp.feat.sniffsubr: A feature bit indicating the device supports the Sniff Subrating feature for additional power saving.
btbrlmp.feat.pauseenc: A feature bit indicating the device supports pausing and resuming encryption on a connection.
btbrlmp.feat.afhcapma: Indicates a master device is capable of performing Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH).
btbrlmp.feat.afhclama: Indicates a master device is capable of classifying channels for AFH.
btbrlmp.feat.esco2: Indicates the device supports 2 Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) for eSCO links.
btbrlmp.feat.esco3: Indicates the device supports 3 Mbps Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) for eSCO links.
btbrlmp.feat.3slotenhesco: Indicates the device supports 3-slot eSCO packets for Enhanced Data Rate (EDR).
btbrlmp.feat.extinqres: A feature bit indicating the device supports providing an Extended Inquiry Response (EIR) packet.
btbrlmp.feat.simlebredr: Indicates the controller can simultaneously maintain LE and BR/EDR connections to the same remote device.
btbrlmp.feat.res3: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.ssp: A feature bit indicating the controller supports Secure Simple Pairing (SSP).
btbrlmp.feat.enpdu: A feature bit indicating the device supports encapsulating data from other protocols within LMP PDUs.
btbrlmp.feat.edr: Indicates the device supports Erroneous Data Reporting, where corrupted but usable data can be passed to the host.
btbrlmp.feat.nonflush: Indicates support for the Non-flushable Packet Boundary Flag, allowing for reliable data transfer.
btbrlmp.feat.res4: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.lstimche: Indicates the controller will send an event when the link supervision timeout is changed.
btbrlmp.feat.inqtxpwr: Indicates the device supports reporting its inquiry transmit power level.
btbrlmp.feat.enhpwr: Indicates the device supports the Enhanced Power Control feature.
btbrlmp.feat.res5: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.res6: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.res7: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.res8: A reserved bit in the feature mask for future use.
btbrlmp.feat.extfeat: A bit indicating that the device supports more features, which are detailed in the 'Extended Features' list.
btbrlmp.featuresext: An extended bitmask representing additional Bluetooth features supported by the device.
btbrlmp.efeat.ssp: An extended feature bit indicating that the Host supports Secure Simple Pairing (SSP).
btbrlmp.efeat.lesup: An extended feature bit indicating that the Host supports Bluetooth Low Energy (LE).
btbrlmp.efeat.lebredr: Indicates the Host can simultaneously handle LE and BR/EDR connections to the same remote device.
btbrlmp.efeat.sch: An extended feature bit indicating that the Host supports Secure Connections for stronger pairing.
btbrlmp.efeat.csbma: Indicates the device supports operating as a master in a Connectionless Slave Broadcast.
btbrlmp.efeat.csbsl: Indicates the device supports operating as a slave in a Connectionless Slave Broadcast.
btbrlmp.efeat.syntr: Indicates the device supports transmitting a Synchronization Train for periodic advertising.
btbrlmp.efeat.synsc: Indicates the device supports scanning for a Synchronization Train for periodic advertising.
btbrlmp.efeat.inqresnote: Indicates the device supports receiving inquiry response results via a notification event.
btbrlmp.efeat.genintsc: Indicates the device supports the Generalized Interlaced Scan feature.
btbrlmp.efeat.ccadj: Indicates the device supports the Coarse Clock Adjustment feature.
btbrlmp.efeat.res0: A reserved bit in the extended features mask for future use.
btbrlmp.efeat.scc: An extended feature bit indicating that the Controller supports Secure Connections.
btbrlmp.efeat.ping: An extended feature bit indicating the device supports the Ping feature to check link responsiveness and authentication.
btbrlmp.efeat.res1: A reserved bit in the extended features mask for future use.
btbrlmp.efeat.trnud: Indicates the device supports the Train Nudging feature for synchronization.
btbrlmp.efeat.sam: Indicates the device supports the Slot Availability Mask feature to coordinate activities between different wireless technologies.
btbrlmp.fpage: The page number of the features mask being requested or reported.
btbrlmp.htime: The requested duration, in time slots, for the connection to remain in Hold mode.
btbrlmp.hinst: The specific clock tick (instant) at which the device will enter Hold mode.
btbrlmp.hopmode: The frequency hopping mode being used, typically either Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH) or the standard 79-channel hopping.
btbrlmp.iocaps: Specifies the Input/Output capabilities of the device (e.g., DisplayOnly, KeyboardOnly) to determine the Secure Simple Pairing method.
btbrlmp.jitter: The maximum random scheduling variation, in microseconds, for an eSCO link.
btbrlmp.key: The encryption key or link key being used or exchanged.
btbrlmp.keysz: The negotiated size of the encryption key, in bytes.
btbrlmp.ksmask: A bitmask indicating the encryption key sizes supported by the device.
btbrlmp.ltaddr: The Logical Transport Address assigned to the device for this piconet.
btbrlmp.maccess: The number of access windows in which a master will listen for a slave in sniff mode.
btbrlmp.maxslots: The maximum number of slots the device is allowed to occupy for a single packet transmission.
btbrlmp.maxsp: The highest page number of the extended features list that contains at least one non-zero bit.
btbrlmp.maxss: The maximum sniff subrate value, in slots, that can be used.
btbrlmp.minsmt: The minimum timeout value, in slots, that can be used in sniff mode.
btbrlmp.naccslots: The number of slots in the access window during sniff mode.
btbrlmp.namefrag: A fragment of the remote device's user-friendly name, as LMP messages have limited size.
btbrlmp.namelen: The total length, in bytes, of the remote device's full name.
btbrlmp.nameoffset: The starting position (offset) of the name fragment within the full device name.
btbrlmp.nb: The number of broadcast retransmissions for a connectionless slave broadcast.
btbrlmp.nbsleep: The sleep duration parameter for a connectionless slave broadcast.
btbrlmp.negstate: Indicates the current state of a negotiation procedure within LMP.
btbrlmp.nonce: A cryptographic nonce (a random or pseudo-random number) used once during pairing or encryption setup to prevent replay attacks.
btbrlmp.nottype: The type of notification being sent in an LMP message, such as a link supervision timeout change.
btbrlmp.npoll: The polling interval, in slots, for a SCO link.
btbrlmp.oobauthdata: Indicates whether Out-of-Band authentication data (e.g., from NFC) is available for pairing.
btbrlmp.op: The Opcode, a numeric value that identifies the specific LMP command being sent (e.g., LMP_setup_complete).
btbrlmp.opinre: The Opcode of the original request that this LMP message is a response to.
btbrlmp.pagesch: The paging scheme and settings being used to establish a connection.
btbrlmp.pcmode: The power control mode, which can be enabled or disabled.
btbrlmp.pkttype: A bitmask representing the packet types (e.g., DM1, DH3, AUX1) that are allowed on the current connection.
btbrlmp.pkttypetbl: The packet type table being used for the logical link.
btbrlmp.pmaddr: The Park Member Address, an 8-bit address assigned to a device when it is in the low-power Park state.
btbrlmp.pollintvl: The interval, in time slots, between consecutive poll attempts by the master.
btbrlmp.pollper: The polling period for a connection, measured in units of 1.25 milliseconds.
btbrlmp.pssettings: The specific settings for the currently active Paging Scheme.
btbrlmp.pwradjreq: A request made by one device to the other to increase or decrease its transmit power.
btbrlmp.pwradjres: The response to a power adjustment request, indicating the change in power level.
btbrlmp.pwradj_8dpsk: The power adjustment response for 8DPSK modulated signals (part of 3-Mbps EDR).
btbrlmp.pwradj_dqpsk: The power adjustment response for DQPSK modulated signals (part of 2-Mbps EDR).
btbrlmp.pwradj_gfsk: The power adjustment response for GFSK modulated signals (Basic Rate).
btbrlmp.rand: A random number exchanged between devices, typically used as a challenge during authentication or to generate encryption keys.
btbrlmp.rate: The data rate being used for the connection.
btbrlmp.rate.fec: Indicates whether Forward Error Correction (FEC) is being used for the packet type.
btbrlmp.rate.size: The size, in bytes, of a Basic Rate (BR) packet.
btbrlmp.rate.type: The type of Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) being used (e.g., 2-DH5, 3-DH5).
btbrlmp.rate.edrsize: The size, in bytes, of an Enhanced Data Rate (EDR) packet.
btbrlmp.rxfreq: The frequency on which the device is currently set to receive, expressed as a MHz offset from the 2402 MHz base.
btbrlmp.scohdl: The handle or identifier for a specific Synchronous Connection-Oriented (SCO) link.
btbrlmp.scopkt: The packet type (e.g., HV1, HV3) being used for a SCO link.
btbrlmp.slotoffset: A timing adjustment value, in microseconds, to align slot boundaries between devices.
btbrlmp.sniffatt: The number of slots a device in sniff mode will listen for a transmission from the master.
btbrlmp.sniffsi: The specific clock tick (instant) at which sniff subrating will begin.
btbrlmp.sniffto: The timeout value, in terms of receive slots, for a sniff attempt.
btbrlmp.subversnr: The subversion number of the Link Manager Protocol (LMP) implementation, specific to the manufacturer.
btbrlmp.suptimeout: The supervision timeout, in slots, after which a link is considered lost if no packets are received.
btbrlmp.swinst: The specific clock tick (instant) at which a master/slave role switch will occur.
btbrlmp.taccess: The timing parameter, in slots, for the access window in Park mode.
btbrlmp.tb: The time interval, in slots, of the broadcast beacon in Park mode.
btbrlmp.tesco: The timing interval, in slots, for an eSCO (extended SCO) link.
btbrlmp.testlen: The length in bytes of the payload for a packet used in a test sequence.
btbrlmp.testscen: Identifies the specific test scenario being run, such as a loopback test or transmitter test.
btbrlmp.tid: A Transaction ID used to match request and response LMP messages.
btbrlmp.timectrl: A set of flags that control timing aspects of the piconet.
btbrlmp.time.change: A timing control flag indicating a change in timing parameters.
btbrlmp.time.init: A timing control flag used during the initialization of the piconet.
btbrlmp.time.accwin: A timing control flag related to the access window in Park mode.
btbrlmp.tsco: The time interval, in slots, for a SCO (Synchronous Connection-Oriented) link.
btbrlmp.tsniff: The interval, in slots, between sniff attempts, defining how often a device wakes up to listen.
btbrlmp.txfreq: The frequency on which the device is currently set to transmit, expressed as a MHz offset from the 2402 MHz base.
btbrlmp.versnr: The version number of the Bluetooth Link Manager Protocol (LMP) specification supported by the device.
T_UINT1: A field in the FHS packet used for filling/padding, also known as FIL.
btl2cap.length: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the payload data immediately following the basic L2CAP header.
btl2cap.cid: The Logical Link Control and Adaptation Protocol (L2CAP) Channel Identifier, which distinguishes between different logical data flows over a single link.
btl2cap.payload: The actual application data or higher-level protocol information being carried within the L2CAP packet.
btl2cap.command: The signaling command being sent over the L2CAP signaling channel.
btl2cap.cmd_code: The specific code that identifies the L2CAP signaling command, such as Connection Request or Configuration Request.
btl2cap.cmd_ident: An identifier used to match a signaling command with its corresponding response.
btl2cap.cmd_length: The length, in bytes, of the data field associated with an L2CAP signaling command.
btl2cap.cmd_data: The data payload of an L2CAP signaling command, containing the parameters for that command.
btl2cap.psm: The Protocol/Service Multiplexer value, which identifies the higher-level protocol (e.g., RFCOMM, SDP) that the L2CAP channel is for.
btl2cap.scid: The Source Channel Identifier, representing the local endpoint of the L2CAP channel.
btl2cap.dcid: The Destination Channel Identifier, representing the remote endpoint of the L2CAP channel.
btl2cap.icid: The Initiator Channel Identifier used in some L2CAP procedures.
btl2cap.ctrl_id: An identifier for the controller that the L2CAP channel is associated with, used in AMP (Alternate MAC/PHY) architectures.
btl2cap.dctrl_id: The identifier for the destination controller in an AMP architecture.
btl2cap.result: A code indicating the outcome of an L2CAP signaling command, such as success, failure, or pending.
btl2cap.move_result: Indicates the outcome of a request to move an L2CAP channel to a different controller.
btl2cap.status: Provides additional information about the result of an L2CAP signaling command.
btl2cap.rej_reason: Specifies the reason why an L2CAP command was rejected, such as PSM not supported or resources unavailable.
btl2cap.sig_mtu: The Maximum Transmission Unit for the signaling channel, defining the largest signaling command that can be sent.
btl2cap.info_mtu: The acceptable connectionless MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) of the remote device.
btl2cap.info_flowcontrol: Indicates whether the remote device supports flow control mode.
btl2cap.info_retransmission: Indicates whether the remote device supports retransmission mode for reliable data transfer.
btl2cap.info_bidirqos: Indicates whether the remote device supports bi-directional Quality of Service (QoS).
btl2cap.info_enh_retransmission: Indicates support for the Enhanced Retransmission Mode, an improved reliability layer in L2CAP.
btl2cap.info_streaming: Indicates support for Streaming Mode, which is a unidirectional, unreliable data transfer mode.
btl2cap.info_fcs: Indicates whether the device supports using a Frame Check Sequence (FCS) for error detection in L2CAP packets.
btl2cap.info_flow_spec: Indicates support for the Extended Flow Specification feature for BR/EDR connections.
btl2cap.info_fixedchan: Indicates support for the Fixed Channels feature, which reserves specific CIDs for common services.
btl2cap.info_window: Indicates support for the Extended Window Size feature in Enhanced Retransmission Mode.
btl2cap.info_unicast: Indicates support for receiving Unicast Connectionless Data.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans: A bitmask indicating which specific fixed channels are supported by the device.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_null: Indicates support for the Null identifier fixed channel.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_signal: Indicates support for the standard L2CAP signaling channel.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_connless: Indicates support for the connectionless reception fixed channel.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_amp_man: Indicates support for the AMP Manager Protocol fixed channel.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_rfu: A reserved bit in the fixed channels mask for future use.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_smp: Indicates support for the BR/EDR Security Manager Protocol fixed channel.
btl2cap.info_fixedchans_amp_test: Indicates support for the AMP Test Manager fixed channel.
btl2cap.info_type: The type of information being requested in an L2CAP Information Request command.
btl2cap.info_result: The result of the L2CAP Information Request, indicating success or failure.
btl2cap.info_extfeatures: A bitmask showing the extended L2CAP features supported by the remote device.
btl2cap.flags.reserved: Reserved bits in the flags field for future use.
btl2cap.flags.continuation: A flag indicating that this L2CAP packet is a continuation of a previous packet.
btl2cap.conf_result: The result of a configuration attempt, such as success, unacceptable parameters, or pending.
btl2cap.option_type: The type of configuration option being negotiated, such as MTU or Flush Timeout.
btl2cap.option_length: The length of the payload for this specific configuration option.
btl2cap.option_mtu: The Maximum Transmission Unit size that the originator of the request can receive on this channel.
btl2cap.option_flushto: The amount of time, in microseconds, that the device will attempt to transmit a packet before discarding it.
btl2cap.option_sdu_size: The Maximum Service Data Unit (SDU) size.
btl2cap.option_sdu_arrival_time: The SDU Inter-arrival Time, used for Quality of Service (QoS) configurations.
btl2cap.option_ident: An identifier for a specific flow specification.
btl2cap.option_access_latency: The maximum time, in microseconds, between a transmission request and the actual transmission, used for QoS.
btl2cap.option_flags: Flags reserved for future use in L2CAP options, which must be set to zero.
btl2cap.option_servicetype: The service level required for the channel, such as 'best effort' or 'guaranteed'.
btl2cap.option_tokenrate: For guaranteed QoS, this is the rate at which data credits are granted in bytes per second.
btl2cap.option_tokenbsize: The size of the 'token bucket' in bytes, used to handle bursts of data in guaranteed QoS.
btl2cap.option_peakbandwidth: The maximum speed, in bytes per second, at which packets may be sent, used for QoS.
btl2cap.option_latency: The maximum acceptable delay for a packet, in microseconds, from sender to receiver.
btl2cap.option_delayvar: The acceptable variance in delay (jitter), in microseconds, for the data flow.
btl2cap.retransmissionmode: The negotiated mode for reliable data transfer, such as Basic, Enhanced Retransmission, or Streaming.
btl2cap.txwindow: The size of the transmission window, indicating how many packets can be sent without receiving an acknowledgment.
btl2cap.maxtransmit: The maximum number of times the device will retransmit an unacknowledged I-frame before terminating the connection.
btl2cap.retransmittimeout: The time, in milliseconds, a device will wait for an acknowledgment before retransmitting a packet.
btl2cap.monitortimeout: The interval, in milliseconds, at which supervisory frames (S-frames) are sent to monitor the link status.
btl2cap.mps: The Maximum PDU Payload Size that the sender can receive on this channel.
btl2cap.option_fcs: The type of Frame Check Sequence (FCS) to be used for error detection on the channel.
btl2cap.option_window: The extended window size for data transmission.
btl2cap.conf_param_option: A parameter or option being negotiated during the channel configuration phase.
btl2cap.control_sar: Indicates the segmentation and reassembly status of the packet (e.g., start, continuation, end, or unsegmented).
btl2cap.control_reqseq: The Request Sequence Number, used to acknowledge received packets in some L2CAP modes.
btl2cap.control_txseq: The Transmit Sequence Number of this frame, incremented for each new data packet sent.
btl2cap.control_retransmissiondisable: A flag to disable retransmissions for this particular frame.
btl2cap.control_supervisory: Identifies the type of supervisory frame being sent, such as Receiver Ready (RR) or Reject (REJ).
btl2cap.control_type: The type of L2CAP frame, such as I-Frame (Information), S-Frame (Supervisory), or U-Frame (Unnumbered).
btl2cap.control: The control word containing various fields like sequence numbers and frame types for advanced L2CAP modes.
btl2cap.fcs: The Frame Check Sequence, a calculated value (like a CRC) used to detect errors in the received L2CAP frame.
btl2cap.sdulength: The total length of the upper-layer Service Data Unit (SDU) before it was fragmented into L2CAP packets.
btl2cap.reassembled_in: A reference to the frame number where the complete Service Data Unit (SDU) has been reassembled.
btl2cap.continuation_to: A reference to the frame number that contains the previous fragment of this Service Data Unit (SDU).
btl2cap.min_interval: The minimum desired connection interval for a Bluetooth Low Energy link.
btl2cap.max_interval: The maximum desired connection interval for a Bluetooth Low Energy link.
btl2cap.peripheral_latency: The number of connection events the slave device is allowed to skip, used for power saving in LE.
btl2cap.timeout_multiplier: A multiplier used with the connection interval to calculate the supervision timeout for an LE link.
btl2cap.le_result: Indicates the result of an LE L2CAP signaling command.
btl2cap.credits: The number of credits being granted to the remote device, allowing it to send a corresponding number of LE data packets.
btl2cap.initial_credits: The number of credits a device is initially given when an LE L2CAP connection-oriented channel is established.
btl2cap.le_psm: The Protocol/Service Multiplexer value used specifically for an LE L2CAP channel, identifying the upper-layer protocol.
btl2cap.data: The data payload being carried by the L2CAP packet.
btl2cap.service: The higher-level service or protocol that is using the L2CAP channel.
btl2cap.connect_in: A reference to the frame number where the connection for this L2CAP channel was initiated.
btl2cap.disconnect_in: A reference to the frame number where the disconnection for this L2CAP channel occurred.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragments: A collection of all the individual fragments that make up a single LE Service Data Unit (SDU).
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment: A single piece of a fragmented LE Service Data Unit (SDU).
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.overlap: Indicates that this SDU fragment partially or completely overlaps with another fragment for the same SDU.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.overlap.conflict: Indicates that two overlapping SDU fragments contain different data, signifying a reassembly error.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.multiple_tails: Indicates that more than one fragment has been marked as the end of the SDU, which is an error condition.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.too_long_fragmen: Indicates that a fragment's length is greater than the total expected SDU length.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.error: A general error detected during the defragmentation of an SDU.
btl2cap.le_sdu.fragment.count: The total number of fragments that constitute the complete SDU.
btl2cap.le_sdu.reassembled.in: A reference to the frame number where all fragments of this SDU were successfully reassembled.
btl2cap.le_sdu.reassembled.length: The total length of the SDU after all its fragments have been reassembled.
btl2cap.le_sdu_length: The length of the complete Service Data Unit (SDU) announced in the first packet of a segmented LE L2CAP transmission.
